name: APA102 addressable LED strip (60 LEDs, 1 m)
description: 1 m flexible strip of 60 APA102C (iPixel/Shiji) RGB LEDs, each with its own 8-bit-per-colour PWM and 5-bit global brightness, driven over a two-wire clock + data (SPI-style) bus with no chip select. Runs on a regulated 5 V to 5.5 V supply; up to 2.88 A per metre at full white. Sold as: SparkFun LED RGB Strip - Addressable, 1m (APA102), COM-14015 (60 LEDs/m, iPixel S60102 strip, pads GND, CI, DI, 5V with 4-pin 0.1" connectors).
eli5: A bendy ribbon of 60 colour lights that you set one by one with a clock wire and a data wire.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the microcontroller and the 5 V supply

pins.name: CI
pins.description: Clock in (strip lead CLK). Data is latched on the rising edge. Input high needs 0.7 x VDD (3.5 V at 5 V).

pins.name: DI
pins.description: Data in (strip lead DAT), MSB first. Input high needs 0.7 x VDD (3.5 V at 5 V).

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: LED supply, regulated 5 V to 5.5 V (5.0 V typical, 5.5 V max per the APA102C datasheet). Up to 2.88 A for 60 LEDs at full white: feed from a separate 5 V supply.

buildNotes: Wire the INPUT end: the arrows printed on the strip point away from it. The pads read GND, CI, DI, 5V; on the iPixel S60102 leads red = 5V, blue = CLK (CI), green = DAT (DI), yellow = GND. Wire colours vary by batch, so go by the printed pads.
Power the strip from a separate 5 V supply rated for at least 3 A (2.88 A per metre at full white) and join its GND to the board's GND. Never exceed 5.5 V (6.0 V absolute maximum).
CI and DI need a high of at least 0.7 x VDD (3.5 V at 5 V). 3.3 V logic often works on short wires but is not guaranteed: add a 74AHCT125 level shifter on CI and DI for a reliable strip.
Frame order per the datasheet: 32 zero bits, then per LED 0b111 + 5-bit brightness, blue, green, red, then the end frame of 1 bits (at least n/2 clock edges for n LEDs).
Put a 1000 uF capacitor across 5V and GND at the strip's input.

driver.code:
# APA102 / APA102C addressable LED strip, MicroPython driver.
# Two-wire synchronous protocol from the iPixel APA102C datasheet:
#   * data (DI) is sampled on the RISING edge of the clock (CI), MSB first -> SPI mode 0
#     (polarity=0, phase=0). No chip select: every byte on the bus goes down the strip.
#   * start frame: 32 zero bits
#   * one 32-bit frame per LED: 0b111 + 5-bit global brightness (0-31), then BLUE, GREEN, RED
#     (8 bits each, 0-255 PWM duty)
#   * end frame: 1 bits. The datasheet shows 32; each LED delays the data by half a clock,
#     so long strips need at least n/2 extra clock edges: we send max(4, ceil(n/16)) bytes of 0xFF.
# Up to 60 mA per LED at full white: keep brightness low on USB power.


class APA102:
    def __init__(self, spi, n, brightness=4):
        self.spi = spi
        self.n = n
        self.brightness = brightness
        self.buf = bytearray(4 * n)
        self.end = b'\xff' * max(4, (n + 15) // 16)
        self.fill((0, 0, 0))

    @property
    def brightness(self):
        return self._gb

    @brightness.setter
    def brightness(self, value):
        """Global brightness 0-31 (5-bit current setting from the datasheet)."""
        self._gb = max(0, min(31, int(value)))

    def __len__(self):
        return self.n

    def __setitem__(self, i, color):
        """color = (r, g, b), 0-255 each. Optional 4th item = per-LED brightness 0-31."""
        r, g, b = color[0], color[1], color[2]
        gb = color[3] if len(color) > 3 else self._gb
        o = 4 * i
        self.buf[o] = 0xE0 | (max(0, min(31, gb)))
        self.buf[o + 1] = b & 0xFF
        self.buf[o + 2] = g & 0xFF
        self.buf[o + 3] = r & 0xFF

    def __getitem__(self, i):
        o = 4 * i
        return (self.buf[o + 3], self.buf[o + 2], self.buf[o + 1])

    def fill(self, color):
        for i in range(self.n):
            self[i] = color

    def show(self):
        self.spi.write(b'\x00\x00\x00\x00')  # start frame
        self.spi.write(self.buf)
        self.spi.write(self.end)

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import sys, time
from apa102 import APA102

# Pico: SPI0 owns SCK GP2/6/18, SPI1 owns GP10/14. ESP32: SPI(1) on any pins.
sid = ({CI} // 8) % 2 if sys.platform == 'rp2' else 1
spi = SPI(sid, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CI}), mosi=Pin({DI}))
strip = APA102(spi, 60, brightness=4)
strip.show()
time.sleep(1)
for i in range(60):
    strip[i] = (255, 0, 0) if i % 2 == 0 else (0, 0, 255)
strip.show()
print('strip lit: 60 LEDs red/blue')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
